source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole bisogna indurre l'infortunato a parlare o a tossire

records.localized_text: With fractured ribs, encourage the casualty to speak or cough.

source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole è necessario mettere la vittima in posizione laterale di sicurezza

records.localized_text: With fractured ribs, place the victim in the recovery position.

source.text_it: In caso di incendio, il soccorritore deve coprire la vittima ustionata con materiale possibilmente sterile per evitare infezioni

records.localized_text: In a fire, cover a burn victim with preferably sterile material to prevent infection.

source.text_it: In caso di incendio, il soccorritore deve evitare di staccare residui di tessuto aderenti alle parti ustionate della vittima

records.localized_text: In a fire, the rescuer must not detach fabric stuck to the victim's burns.

source.text_it: Nel caso di gravi ustioni provocati dalla bruciatura dei vestiti bisogna spogliare immediatamente l'infortunato

records.localized_text: For severe burns caused by burning clothing, the casualty must immediately be undressed.

source.text_it: Il soccorritore deve spegnere le fiamme che avvolgono la vittima soffocandole con una coperta

records.localized_text: The rescuer must extinguish flames surrounding the victim by smothering them with a blanket.

source.text_it: In caso di incendio, il soccorritore deve astenersi dall'intervenire per proteggersi e chiamare i vigili del fuoco

records.localized_text: In a fire, the rescuer must refrain from intervening for self-protection and call the fire brigade.

source.text_it: In caso di incendio, il soccorritore deve bagnare le ustioni con acqua fredda

records.localized_text: In a fire, the rescuer must wet burns with cold water.

source.text_it: In caso di incendio, il soccorritore deve staccare i residui di tessuto aderenti alle parti ustionate della vittima

records.localized_text: In a fire, the rescuer must remove fabric stuck to the victim's burns.

source.text_it: In caso di incendio, il soccorritore deve bagnare le ustioni con acqua calda

records.localized_text: In a fire, the rescuer must wet burns with hot water.

source.text_it: Se la vittima presenta fratture non esposte di un arto non bisogna fare niente, limitarsi solo a spostare l'infortunato

records.localized_text: For a closed limb fracture, do nothing except move the casualty.

source.text_it: Le fratture sono lesioni delle ossa e possono essere composte o scomposte

records.localized_text: Fractures are bone injuries and may be displaced or undisplaced.

source.text_it: Nel caso di frattura l'infortunato non deve essere coperto

records.localized_text: A person with a fracture must not be covered.

source.text_it: Le fratture sono emorragie interne

records.localized_text: Fractures are internal haemorrhages.

source.text_it: Se la vittima presenta fratture di un arto si può tentare di immobilizzare l'articolazione con mezzi di fortuna

records.localized_text: For a limb fracture, one may try to immobilise the joint using improvised means.

source.text_it: Solo le fratture esposte richiedono l'intervento del medico

records.localized_text: Only open fractures require a doctor.

source.text_it: Se la vittima presenta fratture ad un arto, bisogna somministrarle bevande alcoliche

records.localized_text: For a limb fracture, give the victim alcoholic drinks.

source.text_it: Se la vittima presenta fratture ad un arto bisogna misurarle immediatamente la temperatura corporea

records.localized_text: For a limb fracture, immediately measure the victim's body temperature.

source.text_it: Le fratture devono essere coperte con panni sterili, solo se esposte

records.localized_text: Fractures should be covered with sterile cloth only if open.

source.text_it: Le fratture vanno sempre immobilizzate

records.localized_text: Fractures must always be immobilised.

source.text_it: In presenza di frattura non esposta di un arto, bisogna impedire la mobilità dell'arto infortunato

records.localized_text: For a closed limb fracture, prevent movement of the injured limb.

source.text_it: In caso di incidente, non bisogna spostare il ferito se si sospettano lesioni alla colonna vertebrale

records.localized_text: After an accident, do not move an injured person if spinal injury is suspected.

source.text_it: Nel caso di incidente stradale si deve chiamare l'ambulanza, anche se non ci sono feriti

records.localized_text: After a road accident, an ambulance must be called even if nobody is injured.

source.text_it: Quando si verifica un incidente stradale deve essere esibito, tra gli altri, il libretto di uso e manutenzione del veicolo

records.localized_text: When a road accident occurs, the vehicle's use and maintenance manual must be presented among other documents.

source.text_it: Quando si verifica un incidente stradale deve essere esibito, tra gli altri, il certificato di assicurazione

records.localized_text: When a road accident occurs, the insurance certificate must be presented among other documents.

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE: making someone cough or speak is not a general rule after an accident. A suspected rib fracture after a serious accident needs urgent assessment; during recovery, breathing normally and coughing when needed helps clear the lungs. The question does not distinguish these stages.
evidence: NHS, Broken or bruised ribs, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/broken-or-bruised-ribs/: serious accident requires urgent assessment; during recovery normal breathing and coughing when needed clear mucus. The quiz does not identify a care stage; no claim of official intended rationale.

rows.text: The recovery position helps keep the airway open for an unresponsive person breathing normally; a rib fracture alone does not automatically require it. Assess breathing and condition and call for help.
evidence: St John Ambulance, Recovery position: https://www.sja.org.uk/first-aid-advice/recovery-position/ — for an unresponsive person breathing normally.

rows.text: After cooling the burn, cover it loosely with a sterile, non-fluffy dressing if available to protect it from contamination.
evidence: NHS South West Burns Clinical Network, First Aid: https://southwest-burncare-network.nhs.uk/first-aid — cool then cover loosely with sterile non-fluffy dressing.

rows.text: Do not pull off stuck fabric: this can further damage the skin. Remove only clothing that is not attached to the burn.
evidence: NHS, Burns and scalds, first aid: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ — cool with running water, leave stuck clothing and cover after cooling.

rows.text: Do not indiscriminately undress the person: leave clothing stuck to burned skin in place and carefully remove only clothing that is not stuck.
evidence: NHS, Burns and scalds, first aid: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ — cool with running water, leave stuck clothing and cover after cooling.

rows.text: A blanket can smother flames on clothing by cutting off air. Intervene only if it is safe to do so.
evidence: NHS South West Burns Clinical Network, First Aid for Burns and Scalds: https://southwest-burncare-network.nhs.uk/_common/getdocument?id=294981 — smother burning clothing with a blanket; Red Cross, check scene safety: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/articles/the-three-cs-of-first-aid-check-call-care.

rows.text: Calling emergency services matters, but it does not mean withholding all help: provide first aid if the scene is safe. Do not enter a dangerous area.
evidence: American Red Cross, Check, Call, Care: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/articles/the-three-cs-of-first-aid-check-call-care — check safety, call and provide care; https://www.redcross.org/get-help/how-to-prepare-for-emergencies/types-of-emergencies/fire/if-a-fire-starts.html/ — get out, stay out and call.

rows.text: Cool running water cools the burned area and limits heat damage; avoid ice and excessively cold water.
evidence: NHS, Burns and scalds, first aid: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ — cool with running water, leave stuck clothing and cover after cooling. NHS Gateshead, Burns and scalds: https://www.gatesheadhealth.nhs.uk/resources/burns-and-scalds/ — cool running water, not ice.

rows.text: Do not remove stuck fabric: pulling it off can worsen the injury. Leave anything attached to the skin in place.
evidence: NHS, Burns and scalds, first aid: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ — cool with running water, leave stuck clothing and cover after cooling.

rows.text: Hot water does not cool the injury. Use cool running water, not ice, to reduce heat damage.
evidence: NHS, Burns and scalds, first aid: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ — cool with running water, leave stuck clothing and cover after cooling. NHS Gateshead: https://www.gatesheadhealth.nhs.uk/resources/burns-and-scalds/ — cool water, not ice.

rows.text: A closed fracture also needs care: keep the limb still in the position found and seek help, avoiding unnecessary movement or attempts to straighten it.
evidence: American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate.

rows.text: A fracture is a break in a bone. It is nondisplaced when the fragments remain aligned and displaced when they have moved from their normal position.
evidence: MSD Manual, Deciphering Medical Terms for Fractures: https://www.msdmanuals.com/home/multimedia/table/deciphering-medical-terms-for-fractures — displaced versus nondisplaced fragments.

rows.text: A fracture does not prevent covering the person to keep them warm; avoid moving the injured part while helping.
evidence: American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate. American Red Cross, shock care: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/shock — keep the person warm.

rows.text: A fracture is a broken bone, not internal bleeding. However, bleeding and other injuries can accompany a fracture.
evidence: MSD Manual, Overview of Fractures: https://www.msdmanuals.com/home/injuries-and-poisoning/fractures/overview-of-fractures — fractures are broken bones and may cause bleeding.

rows.text: A limb can be supported and immobilized with improvised materials without straightening it, but only if you know how to do so without increasing pain. If help will arrive soon, keep it still in the position found.
evidence: American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate.

rows.text: A closed fracture also needs medical assessment: intact skin does not rule out a broken bone or other complications.
evidence: American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate.

rows.text: Do not give alcohol or other drinks: the person may need anesthesia. Keep the limb still and seek help.
evidence: NHS, broken bone care: https://collingwoodsurgery.nhs.uk/jubilee-park/common-questions/accidents-first-aid-and-treatmentshow-do-i-know-if-i-have-broken-a-bone — avoid food and drink because anaesthesia may be needed; American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate.

rows.text: Taking the temperature immediately is not the priority for a suspected fracture. Assess the person, keep the injured part still and seek help.
evidence: American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate.

rows.text: An open fracture has a wound to protect with a sterile or clean dressing; in a closed fracture the skin is intact and there is no wound over the fracture to cover.
evidence: MSD Manual, fracture terms: https://www.msdmanuals.com/home/multimedia/table/deciphering-medical-terms-for-fractures — open fracture has a wound, closed fracture intact skin; NHS cuts: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — cover wound with sterile gauze or clean cloth.

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE: support depends on the site and circumstances. Keep a suspected injured limb still and supported without straightening it; ribs are not splinted like a limb, and breathing must be preserved. Follow emergency-service instructions.
evidence: NHS, Broken or bruised ribs, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/broken-or-bruised-ribs/: ribs cannot easily be splinted like other bones; normal breathing and necessary coughing during recovery.

American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED participant manual, chapter 6 https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf: keep injured limb still and support it; splint only if trained and no additional pain. No assertion that every fracture requires one method.

rows.text: Keeping the limb still in the position found limits movement at the fracture and the risk of worsening the injury. Do not try to straighten it.
evidence: American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, muscle, bone and joint injuries: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — rest the injured part without moving or straightening it; splint only when appropriate.

rows.text: If you suspect a spinal injury, keep the injured person still and call for help: unnecessary movement can worsen the injury. Follow rescuers’ instructions and act if necessary to save life.
evidence: NHS, First aid: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/first-aid/ — do not move a person with suspected spinal injury unless in immediate danger or necessary for resuscitation.

rows.text: If nobody is injured, an ambulance is not automatically necessary. Stop, make traffic safe and exchange useful information; call medical help if needed.
evidence: Codice della strada, art. 189 commi 1–4: https://aci.gov.it/codice-della-strada/art-189/ — assist injured persons, secure traffic and exchange useful information.

rows.text: The owner’s operation and maintenance manual is not among the traffic documents listed in article 180. After an accident, provide affected people with identification and useful information.
evidence: Codice della strada, artt. 180 comma 1 e 189 comma 4: https://aci.gov.it/codice-della-strada/art-180/ e https://aci.gov.it/codice-della-strada/art-189/ — required documents and exchange of useful information.

rows.text: The insurance certificate is among the documents to carry while driving and contains information useful for compensation. After an accident, provide useful information to affected people.
evidence: Codice della strada, artt. 180 comma 1 lettera d e 189 comma 4: https://aci.gov.it/codice-della-strada/art-180/ e https://aci.gov.it/codice-della-strada/art-189/ — insurance certificate carried and useful information supplied.

source_access_notes: Independently inspected NHS broken ribs and burn guidance, NHS South West Burns Clinical Network first-aid page and actual one-page blanket guidance, Red Cross fracture manual, NHS primary-care broken bone guidance, and ACI CdS arts.180/189. 31700 preserves FALSO while distinguishing accident assessment from necessary coughing during recovery; 31719 avoids conflating limb stabilization and rib splinting, with breathing preserved.

issues.reason: The printed FALSO rejects inducing the injured person to speak or cough after rib fracture, but clinical guidance explicitly encourages coughing as part of rib injury care. The wording does not distinguish immediate accident-scene first aid from later recovery, so the intended scope and verdict need independent adjudication.
checked_sources: Official cqc_nuovo quiz PDF SHA-256 8b95f4871dca30158981ec25c816f2a148eb2f5cb8fcdcad8de52f8d271d1cc6, page index 20, question 31700: prints FALSO.
NHS, Broken or bruised ribs, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/broken-or-bruised-ribs/ — breathe normally and cough when needed to clear mucus.
Leeds Teaching Hospitals, Rib Injuries, https://www.leedsth.nhs.uk/patients/resources/rib-injuries/ — advises trying to breathe deeply and cough to keep the chest clear.

issues.reason: The printed FALSO rejects the unqualified statement that fractures should always be immobilized. Sources support keeping injured limbs still and explain that ribs are not splinted, but absence of a splint does not by itself prove that immobilization is inappropriate; the intended exception cannot be established without inference.
checked_sources: Official cqc_nuovo quiz PDF SHA-256 8b95f4871dca30158981ec25c816f2a148eb2f5cb8fcdcad8de52f8d271d1cc6, page index 20, question 31719: prints FALSO.

American Red Cross, First Aid/CPR/AED Participant’s Manual, chapter 6, https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/no-index/First%20Aid-CPR-AED-Participant%27s-Manual.pdf — keep an injured limb still; splinting depends on circumstances.
NHS, Broken or bruised ribs, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/broken-or-bruised-ribs/ — ribs cannot easily be splinted; this does not establish a general exception to immobilization.
